title: A Siegel period matrix with the full vanishing and nonvanishing theta-constant pattern (3.3)–(3.4) for the specified special fundamental system is a hyperelliptic Jacobian
author: Alessio Fiorentino; Riccardo Salvati Manni
difficulty_reason: The author must turn a prescribed theta-null pattern into a nondegenerate family of multisecants of the Kummer variety, including the general-position condition that an abstract Jacobian criterion requires. The proof differentiates the relevant Frobenius relation into cubic identities and computes a quarter-period Gram matrix whose rank proves that condition in every genus. This is a substantive theta-function and abelian-variety argument beyond ordinary doctoral qualifying material.
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 057, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.057; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete Theorem 4.2 proof on pp.12–13 and the new Frobenius-to-cubic derivation in Proposition 3.9 were read with the exact theta-pattern definitions (3.1)–(3.4). The author obtains the translated Kummer-vector dependence, explicitly computes its bilinear Gram matrix at the chosen quarter-period and proves its rank is g+1, checks irreducibility using the nonvanishing characters, and finishes with Gunning’s established multisecant criterion and Abel’s theorem for the distinct two-torsion points. The Heisenberg-module map and derivative inverse in Proposition 2.2 are recalled in the section explicitly following van Geemen [21], not presented as a new missing core. Gunning’s criterion is prior background; the new verification of its hypotheses is supplied. The broader vanishing-only statements and low-genus experiments are not selected.

statement_scope: Exactly Theorem 4.2: tau in Siegel upper half-space H_g, with the characteristic system m_j of (3.1), B={1,...,2g+1,infinity}, U={g+1,...,2g+1}, and m_T=sum_{j in T}m_j for even subsets T modulo complementation. For every such T, theta_{m_T}(tau,0) vanishes if #(T symmetric-difference U)!=g+1 and is nonzero if that cardinality equals g+1. Then the ppav is the Jacobian of a hyperelliptic curve. The nonvanishing conditions are essential and are explicitly retained; vanishing-only or a lone quartic identity is not the selected statement.
